prize_parts.citation: for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand breaks, through engineered deaminase-nickase fusions
for the concept and demonstration of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, recruiting an E3 ubiquitin ligase to a target with a heterobifunctional molecule

statement.case_for: I keep the same configuration as in round 1, and the exchange has made me more, not less, confident in it. Both parts pass my game-changer test: a simple chemical idea, a clear and quantifiable mechanism, independent replication, and consequences that were not available before. In base editing the idea is deamination of a defined base by an engineered enzyme tethered to a programmable nickase, so that one base pair is changed without a double-strand break or donor template; the evolved adenine deaminase is the part that cannot be dismissed as old chemistry. In degradation the idea is that a molecule that only binds can be made to remove its target, which reaches proteins without an active site, and the ternary-complex energetics are exactly the kind of mechanism that connects to quantitative experiment. Six of eight members carry B024 and four carry this precise pair, but I rest on the science, not the count. The union is three people, which is the only way to carry two achievements, and I think two achievements with separate, clean citations is a stronger statement than a one-part prize that uses all three seats on trainees and a PI for one tool.
statement.case_against: The cost is real and I will not hide it. Komor and Gaudelli wrote the decisive first-author papers, and Gaudelli's evolved deaminase is the clearest new chemistry in the field; a Liu-only credit understates them, and the citation cannot fix that completely. Kondo and Nishida reported Target-AID at about the same time, and I still have not seen a priority record that settles it. On degradation, no PROTAC is an approved drug, Sakamoto and Kim are the first authors of the 2001 paper, and Handa, Ito, Ciulli and Gray hold the cereblon, glue and VHL branches. Base editing may also be read as a follow-on to the 2020 prize. If the committee judges that the Liu-only credit is indefensible, the honest fallback is a one-part base-editing prize, not a quietly enlarged one.

responses.point: Chabes proposes Liu, Komor and Gaudelli as a one-part base-editing prize and argues that Gaudelli's evolved deaminase is the clearest piece of new chemistry and that dropping the two first authors understates it.
responses.response: This is the strongest argument against my configuration and I weigh it seriously, particularly the point about the evolved TadA, which I said in round 1 is the real chemistry. It does not change my vote because the question is what the second seat is worth: the trio spends the whole prize on one tool, while Liu alone allows a second chemical achievement of comparable consequence. The priority claim of Komor and Gaudelli is real, but they were trainees in a programme Liu conceived and directed through the follow-on editors, and the citation can name the engineered deaminase-nickase architecture so that their work is visible even if their names are not. If a majority decides the Liu-only credit is untenable, I would then support your single-part trio over my pairing, because Kondo and Nishida do not displace either of them in my reading of the record: Target-AID is a real precedent for cytidine deamination but was not the general, evolved family of editors.

responses.point: Somfai pairs B003 palladium-catalysed C-N coupling with base editing credited to Liu alone, and argues that base editing is largely protein engineering and directed evolution on top of CRISPR and that PROTAC mechanism is biology.
responses.response: I take B003 seriously and keep it as my first alternative: attribution is clean and maturity is beyond doubt. My difficulty is the same one you name, that the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Kosugi precursor make it look incremental next to two newer capabilities, and your own pairing would mix a synthetic method with a genome tool without a common thread. On your objection to base editing, I disagree that evolution makes it not chemistry: choosing a nucleobase reaction, engineering an enzyme to carry it out on DNA, and coupling it to a nickase so the cell's repair fixes the change is design of a chemical transformation. On PROTACs I side with Brzezinski, since the design of a heterobifunctional molecule and its ternary complex is chemistry acting on a biological pathway.

responses.point: Brzezinski supports the same pairing with Liu, Crews and Deshaies, and argues that Handa's cereblon work belongs to the molecular-glue lineage and should not be merged into the heterobifunctional PROTAC citation.
responses.response: You persuaded me on this in round 1 and I have not moved back. I had raised shifting to Handa if the glue lineage were the mature core, but the glue branch was largely understood mechanistically after the fact, whereas the 2001 Crews and Deshaies work is a designed concept that was then demonstrated, and merging the two histories would make the citation muddy. I do keep one reservation you share, which is that the absence of an approved PROTAC means I rest the citation on the concept and its mechanistic validation, not on therapies, and I would word it that way.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, proposes the same two parts and asks whether a Liu-only credit is defensible and what the citation would say about the decisive first-author papers.
responses.response: My answer to the chair's question is that Liu alone is defensible but only if the citation is written about the principle and the engineered editors rather than about one lab's constructs, so that the evolved deaminase and the double-strand-break-free outcome are the recognised achievement. I would also want the committee to see the Target-AID record before the final ballot, since I think it changes the wording more than the names. I agree with you that the old deamination chemistry is not the new part and would not defend base editing on that ground.

responses.point: Sparr proposes ionizable lipid nanoparticles alone (Cullis, Hope, Madden), on the pKa-tuned charge and non-bilayer phase behaviour argument and clinical validation, and discloses her proximity to the field.
responses.response: The physical chemistry is elegant and I keep B013 as an alternative for that reason, and I appreciate the disclosure. What stops me from preferring it is attribution: a trio of Cullis, Hope and Madden leaves out the ionizable-lipid chemists whose lipids set the potency, such as MacLachlan, and Anderson and Langer, and the committee has said it cannot say whether the lipid or the formulation process carries priority. After 2023 it also risks reading as delivery engineering. If base editing and degradation both fail to reach a majority I would move to B013, but I would want the credit question answered first.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept Liu alone for B024, or will find the omission of Komor and Gaudelli untenable and require a one-part trio.
The documented priority record for Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) relative to Komor et al. 2016 and Gaudelli et al. 2017, which I cannot verify and which may change the citation wording or the names.
Whether crediting the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) rather than the cereblon glue lineage (Handa) is the right core, and how much weight the absence of an approved PROTAC drug should carry.
Whether base editing will be read as a distinct achievement or as a follow-on to the 2020 genome-editing prize.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict has arisen in the first round and I have no recusal to declare. I have no collaboration or institutional tie to Liu, Crews, Deshaies, Handa or any other named candidate; my Warshel and EVB background and my interest in biomolecular simulation are not tied to any shortlisted work. I note that Peter Brzezinski has served with me on the committee since 2015, which is not a conflict for any candidate.
